messages:
Maya Patel: Heads-up — seeing a big retry spike (~4x) against svc/model-serving in us-west2. CPU on the GPU nodes is fine but conn/retries are mostly hitting pods on node-gpu-a-1 while other endpoints get almost no traffic. Likely intra-cluster routing issue (IPVS) after last night's infra changes. Anyone around?

Sam R.: Oof. Can you paste ipvs stats + endpoints? Also which kube-proxy version are we on across nodes?

Maya Patel: Quick snippets: 
```
# ipvsadm -Ln --stats
TCP  10.10.50.12:8080 rr
  -> 10.2.3.11:8080             Masq    1000   120000
  -> 10.2.3.12:8080             Masq      12     1000
  -> 10.2.3.13:8080             Masq     10      800

# kubectl get endpoints svc/model-serving -o wide
addresses: 10.2.3.11,10.2.3.12,10.2.3.13

# top on 10.2.3.11
GPU0  95% utilization  conn-count ~40k
# dmesg | grep rdma
rdma: device mlx5_0: port 1: link down, falling back to TCP
```
Looks like one endpoint with huge conn counts. kernel logs show RDMA -> TCP fallbacks on nodes in the same pool.

Lee Cho: Two things that jumped out: 1) We recently applied MTU change to 9000 on the gpu-pool NICs (aimed at throughput). If some nodes stayed at 1500, IP fragmentation / path MTU mismatches + RDMA fallbacks can cause asymmetric routing. 2) Did kube-proxy roll across all nodes cleanly? IPVS tables can get stale if kube-proxy instances are out-of-sync.

Jamal: Saw kube-proxy crashloop on two gpu nodes around the same time as the kernel update. kube-proxy logs show frequent ipvs sync errors: 
```
E0306 02:14:11.123 kube-proxy.go:998] sync failed: unable to update ipvs service: write ipvs entry: invalid argument
```
We also had a mix of kube-proxy 1.26.3 and 1.25.9 running due to partial upgrade. That mismatch plus the MTU tweak could explain the skewed hashing / local-connection funnels.

Sam R.: Good find. Can we try: 1) run `ipvsadm -Ln --stats` across all nodes to find skewed conn counts, 2) check `kubectl get pods -o wide -n kube-system -l k8s-app=kube-proxy` for versions, 3) check `ethtool -i` and `ip link show` MTU on each NIC? If RDMA falling back, check `dmesg` for mlx5 warnings.

Maya Patel: Running the checks now. Preliminary: two gpu nodes had MTU still at 1500 (ops change didn't roll). kube-proxy versions on those nodes were 1.25.9 and they were the ones with ipvs restart flapping.

Maya Patel: Action taken: cordoned node-gpu-a-1 and node-gpu-a-2, restarted kube-proxy on both, and rolled the MTU to 9000 consistently across the pool. Also forced ipvs sync with: 
```
kubectl -n kube-system delete pod -l k8s-app=kube-proxy
# wait for restarts
ipvsadm -Ln --stats | grep model-serving
```
Traffic instantly smoothed out — connection distribution across endpoints normalized and retry rate dropped back to baseline (~10% -> 2%). :tada:

Lee Cho: Nice. Root cause looks like a combination: partial MTU change causing fragmentation/rdma fallback + kube-proxy version mismatch causing ipvs table desync and uneven hashing weights. We should add a post-upgrade check to validate MTU and kube-proxy rollout.

Jamal: I'll open an incident ticket and follow-up runbook. Suggest we add a preflight for MTU parity across GPU pools and a kube-proxy version gating step in the node-upgrade job.

ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-454 — "ep-conn-walkback / model-serving retry surge" — assigned to eng-infra, severity: P2.

Maya Patel: Thanks — can we also add a Grafana alert for per-endpoint conn skew (if any endpoint has >3x mean conn count)? That would've tripped earlier.

Sam R.: Good call. I'll add a panel + alert with a 10m window and notify #oncall. Quick checklist for postmortem: rollout timeline for MTU change, kube-proxy version matrix, kernel/driver updates (mlx5), ipvs logs.

Maya Patel: Agreed. Leaving nodes cordoned until we validate node-agent health, then will uncordon. Thanks all for the fast responses. :thumbsup:
